newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean ruling party head at strike headquarters.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean ruling party head at strike headquarters.

text.p: South Korea's ruling party head made a dramatic visit to a Seoul cathedral where leaders of a militant union body are directing nationwide strikes, witnesses said.

However, Lee Hong-koo failed at first to meet heads of the Korean Confederation of Trade Unions and instead held talks with the Roman Catholic cardinal of South Korea ahead of all-out work stoppages scheduled to begin on Tuesday.
Later, a union official said strike leaders would only speak with Lee if the government revoked a labour law that has sparked industrial unrest and withdrew arrest warrants against them.
"I'm sorry and embarrassed for causing you trouble," Lee told Cardinal Kim Soo-hwan.

The cardinal replied: "I understand you have passed a law to save the economy, but I hope we all understand that to love this country we have to increase the quality of life for workers as well as save the economy".
Confederation leaders have been sheltering on cathedral grounds to escape arrest, directing strikes from a ramshackle tent in freezing conditions. REUTER
